notes:
Summary: Lighthouse runs an 24/7 helpline used by national utilities. Primary pain: burst incidents during outages -> queue blowups + agent overload. They want agent-assist + automated ticket drafting + safe tool-calls (CRM updates) while guaranteeing SLA during seasonal storms. Requirements highlights:
- Workload profile: baseline 600 concurrent chats, typical day peaks 2.8k concurrent chats during incidents; expected burst factor up to 6x for 15–90 minutes.
- Latency SLO: 95p end-to-end response < 700ms for short agent prompts; prefer sub-200ms per-token generation for assistant flows.
- Throughput: sustain 1.5k reqs/s steady, absorb bursts to 9k reqs/s with graceful degradation.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate (wants predictable committed capacity, willing to pay for Dedicated if fallbacks are clear).
- Model preferences: open Llama-family + Redwood-verified quantized variants; fallback to smaller q4/q8 variants and cached responses for repetitive flows.
- Routing: region-aware routing (US primary, EU for EU customers), auto-fallback to reserve pool when latency degrades.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML & SCIM), audit logs for agent actions, KMS for keys, transcripts retention policy (30/180/365 options), data residency toggles.
User quotes: "During storms our queues triple in 10 minutes — we need predictable behavior, not just 'best effort' AI." — Head of Ops
POC asks: run 2-week POC on Dedicated with simulated 6x burst tests, include KV/prefix caching behavior, tool-calling sandbox to CRM (mock), show blocking/rollback behavior on failed tool calls.
Notes style: shorthand from calls preserved. Priorities: spike reliability > accuracy > unit cost.
Staging: evaluation -> procurement on success.
